newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Jet fuel offered down sharply.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Jet fuel offered down sharply.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel swaps were offered down sharply late afternoon on Wednesday in quiet trade on market expectations of reduced prompt physical buying interest, traders said.
"The regrade (jet fuel/gas oil spread) is being offered down aggressively and there are no buyers around," one broker said.
Balance February regrade was offered down to $3.90 per barrel from Tuesday's $4.30/$4.70 with no firm buying levels seen, brokers said.
March regrade fell slightly and was last quoted at $2.40/$2.70 per barrel, down from Tuesday's $2.50/$2.90.
Brokers said March traded outright earlier today at $27.80 per barrel which gives an implicit regrade value of about $2.30 per barrel. The market traded last night at $2.60 per barrel.
Gas oil swaps were drifting sideways in quiet trade as the market looked to the physical players for direction.
March gas oil swaps were last quoted largely unchanged from Tuesday at $25.30/$25.50 per barrel with no trades confirmed, they said.
Traders said recent exports to India and signs that China may emerge to buy soon,, has led to some optimism but this is countered by persistent physical offers by a local trader.

On Tuesday, the trader sold a 150,000-barrel cargo at $25.10 per barrel free-on-board Singapore, 20 cents below the level traded on Thursday, the last trading day before the long holiday weekend in Singapore.
Fuel oil swaps were also unchanged in thin trading with March seen at $101.00/$102.00 per tonne.
